sources.entry: keras - A high-level deep learning library with support for JAX, TensorFlow, and PyTorch backends.

summary.one_liner: Keras 3 is a high-level deep learning library that runs on JAX, TensorFlow, PyTorch, or OpenVINO (inference only) as interchangeable backends.
summary.what_it_does: Keras 3 provides a high-level API for building and training deep learning models for computer vision, natural language processing, audio, time series forecasting, and recommender systems. The backend is selected with the KERAS_BACKEND environment variable or ~/.keras/keras.json, and can be "tensorflow", "jax", "torch", or "openvino". The OpenVINO backend supports model.predict() only. Keras models can be used inside native TF, JAX, or PyTorch training loops or as part of a PyTorch Module or JAX model function. Models can consume tf.data.Dataset pipelines or PyTorch DataLoaders regardless of backend. The README describes it as a drop-in replacement for tf.keras when using the TensorFlow backend, and saving uses the .keras format. Keras 2 remains available as the separate tf-keras package. An optional gcs extra enables gs:// paths without TensorFlow.
use_cases: build and train neural networks in Python
switch between JAX, TensorFlow and PyTorch backends
time series forecasting with deep learning
migrate existing tf.keras code to a multi-backend setup
how_to_run: pip install tensorflow  (or jax, or torch; install at least one backend)
python pip_build.py --install  (for local development install from source)
conda create -y -n keras-jax python=3.10 && pip install -r requirements-jax-cuda.txt  (optional GPU setup)
notable: Same high-level Keras API runs on JAX, TensorFlow, PyTorch, or OpenVINO backends
Keras models can be embedded in native PyTorch Modules or JAX model functions
Accepts tf.data.Dataset and PyTorch DataLoader inputs with any backend
Drop-in replacement for tf.keras with TensorFlow backend
Separate CUDA requirements files for each backend
caveats: OpenVINO backend is inference-only (model.predict()), no training
Windows is not directly supported; the README recommends WSL2
Backend must be set before importing keras and cannot be changed afterward
